cross_platform_control.differs: GPU model and memory, VBIOS, host CPU model and core count, host memory, instance preset
cross_platform_control.matches: NVIDIA driver 580.173.02, vLLM-Omni runtime 0.25.0 read from the server log on both sides, container image digest sha256:6d2630c7d637b699557573f2c3fee8df5d4d0cd718977aa22549ed6a6ef30587, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NCCL 2.28.9, transformers 5.13.0, Docker 29.7.0, Ubuntu 24.04, model snapshot e0262be9d8f7586bc24c069a2aed2b665bdff266, workload, seed cycle, guardrail posture, and sync timeout

scope: One eight-GPU H200 node, all seven cells measured on the same node under one driver and one container image. The four concurrency-one arrangements ran first, then the two concurrency-two counterparts, then a delayed repeat of the 1 x 8 cell 13.4 hours after the original. Replicas inside each arrangement were active concurrently. Fixed 1280x720, 189-frame, 24 fps, 35-step workload at BF16, guardrails disabled, seeds 17/23/41. Latency is reported as the mean, because each concurrency-two cell is bimodal: the second request arriving at a service waits for the first, so a median falls in the empty gap between the two groups and describes no request that ran. The concurrency-one cells are unimodal, so mean and median agree there. TP-1 is feasible on this node: the model loads at 120.9 GiB against 140.4 GiB usable, leaving about 19 GiB, so the 8 x 1 arrangement is measurable on H200 rather than memory-blocked.
technical_validity_evidence: All 168 production attempts across the seven cells passed reproduce/validate-video.py: complete decode, 1280x720, exactly 189 frames, 24 fps, duration near 7.875 s, not blank, not frozen. Source MP4 SHA-256 values matched, and the byte counts matched the recorded values. The generated clips are not distributed.
